name: High Power Electric Device
description: A self-propelled vehicle, other than a motor vehicle that must be titled and registered, whose electric motor can carry it past 20 mph on motor power alone, including any e-bike tampered with beyond its factory speed or power settings or modified to exceed 20 mph on the motor.

restrictions.rule: Powered by an electric motor capable of more than 20 mph on motor power alone (Utah Code §41-6a-102)

An e-bike with equipment modified or tampered with beyond the manufacturer's settings to change its speed or power output, or made to exceed 20 mph on motor power alone, becomes one (Utah Code §41-6a-102)
Ridden under every traffic-code rule that applies to a motorcycle operator (Utah Code §41-6a-1511)
Riders under 16 may not ride one on a highway, and the owner may not let them (Utah Code §41-6a-1511)
Riders 16 and older may ride one on a highway with a class D driver license and no motorcycle endorsement
Riders under 21 must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218 on a highway
The Driver License Division says it must be street-legal (lights, mirrors and other equipment) and registered with the Division of Motor Vehicles to ride on public roads
One without a VIN that isn't a motorcycle doesn't need liability insurance (Utah Code §41-6a-1511)
Never allowed on a freeway (Utah Code §41-6a-1511)
Local authorities and state agencies may regulate or ban it on sidewalks, paths and trails they control (Utah Code §41-6a-1511)
Commercial sellers must tell buyers the state's insurance and registration requirements (Utah Code §41-6a-1511, enacted by H.B. 381 (2026))
A peace officer who sees a rider under 18 commit a violation may hold it and release it only to a parent or guardian
